- [ ] Investigate this statement: "The existing mutation lock under .git is also questionable and should eventually move behind a proper lock abstraction."
- [ ] Fix .git isolation in orka project:
  - Agents can currently do whatever to the shared git state since all of project .git is mounted rw.
  - Possibly introduce MCP or other specific tooling to let the agent do git actions without actual access to the raw .git dir.
- [ ] Should be able to specify some part of some file for a change.
  The node created for that work should be associated with the node which created that output.
- [x] View a typed turn answer in the Styra interface.
  `Ctrl-T` in the message box cycles the shape the next reply is asked for,
  shown on the box while it applies; `X` opens the answer view, which renders
  `files` as a navigable list (`e` opens the selected location), `lines` as a
  list, `json` pretty-printed, and `text` as prose. `T`/`L`/`F`/`J` re-read the
  same reply under another contract, `R` under the one the turn was sent with.
  A reply that missed its contract is shown as the message plus the reason, not
  an error on its own — `Answer` carries `value: Option<_>` and `error` for
  exactly that.
- [x] Let a queued message carry a return contract.
  The queue holds `QueuedMessage { text, contract }` rather than bare strings,
  so a shape chosen while the agent was busy is still asked for when the queue
  drains. Queue files written before contracts existed load as untyped.
- [ ] Decide what a typed turn should look like in the timeline.
  The server frames the message before recording it, so the event list shows
  the operator's text followed by the whole instruction block. That is honest —
  it is what was sent — but it is roughly ten lines of boilerplate per typed
  turn. Either fold the instructions behind the entry's expansion, or record
  the operator's own text and mark the entry as typed, showing the framing on
  request (`contract::instructions` reproduces it exactly).
